name: fabfilter-promb-drum-deharsh
description: Dynamic presence/harshness control on FabFilter Pro-MB, headless. ONE compression band over ~3-9 kHz that ducks the harsh presence region ONLY when it spikes above threshold, leaving the lows and steady top untouched (true band-split dynamic EQ — Pro-MB's core trick). The drum-bus de-harsh / de-ess move. Validated on the Watercolors drum loop. Reproducible because (a) Pro-MB's bare load is a TRUE passthrough (all 6 bands default Unused — measured 0.00 dB vs input, so unlike Pro-Q you do NOT flatten first) and (b) it sets band_1_state=Enabled AND a NONZERO band_1_range (the master 'amount' knob — at range 0 a band does nothing no matter the threshold/ratio, measured).
intended_for: a drum bus / drum loop / bright bus that gets harsh or spitty in the 3-9 kHz presence band on loud hits, where a static EQ cut would dull the steady top
plugin_build: FabFilter 'Pro-MB.vst3' (renders headless via Pedalboard 0.9.23, no-iLok; all 156 params are Pedalboard valid_values lists settable via setattr — numeric snap to grid, string enums exact)
notes: RANGE IS THE MASTER KNOB: band_1_range must be NONZERO or the band does nothing — measured: a band Enabled with threshold -35 / ratio 4:1 but range 0 == the dry input bit-for-bit. range is the MAX gain change (negative = downward, i.e. compress above threshold here). threshold and ratio only shape HOW it reaches that range.

NO NEED TO FLATTEN: unlike FabFilter Pro-Q (whose bare load restores the last GUI curve), Pro-MB's bare load is a true passthrough — all 6 band slots default to Unused (band_N_state). So a fresh instance + this one Enabled band is clean; you do not have to disable the other bands.

WHY THE HARNESS, NOT apply-vst-chain: every Pro-MB param is an enum (valid_values). apply-vst-chain's float-only dict can set the NUMERIC ones (range/threshold/crossover) but CANNOT set the STRING enums band_1_state / band_1_dynamics_mode / band_1_ratio / the slopes / processing_mode, and cannot ENABLE a band. Measured: setting band_1_range/threshold/crossover via apply-vst-chain returned changed:false (band stayed Unused). Use this harness (setattr) or a dumped state_path.

ATTACK/RELEASE are exposed as a normalized 0..100 scale (NOT ms) on this Pedalboard build (default 20). 8/35 here = fairly fast attack to catch transient harshness, medium release. Knee 12 (soft) for a gentle, dynamic-EQ-like duck. lookahead 2 ms (global lookahead_enabled true) so the duck starts slightly before the transient.

Dynamic Phase (default) keeps near-linear-phase magnitude with low latency and no pre-ring — right for drum transients. Switch to Minimum Phase for lowest latency, or Linear Phase only when phase coherence across a parallel sum matters.

Verify with measure-spectrum: expect a lower spectral centroid + steeper (more negative) tilt and 3-9 kHz pulled down a few dB ON PEAKS while sub/low are untouched (band-split). Push band_1_range more negative or threshold lower for a stronger duck. For de-ESS specifically, narrow to ~5-9 kHz.
